prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a general, ligand-controlled method that turned aryl amine construction from a substrate-limited problem into a routine operation, used daily in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. It is molecular chemistry in the strict sense: the advance came from mechanistic understanding of oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination and from rational ligand design, and it is reproduced and industrially validated over about three decades. Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, broadly applicable versions independently and in parallel, which gives a clean two-person attribution with no need to cut deserving people out arbitrarily. Nothing about maturity or priority is open in the way it is for the biology-adjacent entries.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that the 2010 prize already honoured palladium cross-coupling, so a committee may see C-N coupling as an extension of a recognised family rather than a new concept; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling also complicates the priority narrative. Against that, B057 and B054 open entirely new chemistry-to-biology capabilities, and the opening ballots show B057 has by far the broadest support. I cannot claim that my own methodology background is neutral, and I should be honest that synthetic efficiency is the criterion I weight most heavily.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation is a conceptually original modality that bridges molecular design and biology and reaches previously undruggable targets; Crews, Deshaies and Handa best span concept and mechanism.
responses.response: I agree the concept is original and that B057 is a serious candidate, which is why I ranked it second. My reservation is attribution and timing, not merit. Handa's cereblon work and the Crews-Deshaies PROTAC concept are two different discoveries, one mechanistic and one design-driven, and the eight credited names cannot be fairly compressed into three. With no approved degrader drug, I would be more comfortable letting the field settle than forcing an arbitrary trio now.

responses.point: Degraders connect to ubiquitin-proteasome biochemistry and the thalidomide puzzle, and the first clinical data plus strong confirmation across labs make timing acceptable, though approval is lacking.
responses.response: The thalidomide-cereblon explanation is a real scientific payoff, but it is a mechanistic finding about a drug, and the prize configuration has to decide whether it honours that or the bifunctional design strategy. Dr Chabes treats Crews, Deshaies and Handa as spanning both; I see a split that a three-name limit makes awkward. Pending approvals also mean the therapeutic claim rests on trials, whereas C-N coupling has three decades of verified delivery.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello dynamics is a clean two-person, overdue computational prize, and Pd C-N coupling ranks second only because of his own field bias.
responses.response: I appreciate that Dr Aqvist ranks B068 second and acknowledges the 2010 prize and Kosugi as the points to weigh. On B037 I agree the origin is unambiguous and the maturity is excellent; I simply judge breadth of daily chemical use as favouring C-N coupling. I would not oppose B037 on merit, but it drew only one first-place vote and little else, so I doubt it can reach five votes.

responses.point: Genetic code expansion gave a general chemical handle on protein structure and function, is mature after two decades, and fits a three-person Schultz, Chin, Wang configuration.
responses.response: This is the strongest biology-facing alternative in my view, which is why I ranked it third and name it as an alternative. I qualify it on attribution: Mehl and Yokoyama are real contributors and the orthogonal-pair idea has several roots, so the three-name configuration leaves unresolved credit. I also think the framing question, whether this is chemistry rather than biology, is more open than for a cross-coupling method.

responses.point: Pd C-N coupling is a general, durable method, and the two-person Hartwig-Buchwald configuration is cleanest, with Kosugi a precursor rather than the general catalytic method.
responses.response: I agree and would add that Kosugi's tin-amide reaction required stoichiometric toxic organotin reagents and was narrow in scope, so the general catalytic amine coupling is properly credited to Buchwald and Hartwig. I share her concern that the 2010 prize may weigh against us, but that prize recognised C-C bond formation, and the C-N and C-O variants are distinct in mechanism and consequence.

uncertainties: Whether a majority will accept C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Weight to give Kosugi's precursor work, which cannot be resolved from the supplied record.
Whether B057 can be given a defensible three-person configuration that separates PROTAC design from the cereblon glue mechanism, and whether clinical evidence is sufficient yet.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: none of the shortlisted candidates is listed as a Lund, KTH, Chalmers or Tartu colleague, collaborator or from the Masamune school. As the only synthetic organic chemist on the committee I note a disciplinary preference for B068, which is a bias rather than a recusal matter.
